topics.topic: Define the complete contracts, validation, results, and session effects for MCP discovery methods initialize, ping, and tools/list
questions: What exact inputs, outputs and post-depth validation/error rules apply to `initialize`, `ping` and `tools/list`?
Does `initialize` change connection/session state, negotiate capabilities or gate later discovery and catalogue calls, or is it a stateless informational response?

What are the exact request fields, responses, protocol-version behavior, state effects and post-depth validation/errors for each discovery method, given that they name no catalogue operation and therefore have no operation schema in State 5?
What inputs, outputs, protocol-version negotiation, errors and protocol/session effects do `initialize` and `ping` have?

After those three checks, are `initialize`, `ping` and `tools/list` also checked against method-specific schemas, including rejection of unknown fields, or must every well-formed request from a known token be answered?
What exact result shape, operation order and pagination or cursor behavior must `tools/list` use, and does “every” require the complete catalogue in one response?

quotes: answer_request: [BEHAVIOR] The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, parsed only after the depth check, which follows the size and token checks. A JSON object whose jsonrpc is "2.0" with a string method and an id is a request; one with a method and no id is a notification and one with no method a response: both are answered with empty bytes and change nothing. A request's method decides: initialize answers the result {protocolVersion: the imported MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION constant, capabilities: {tools: {listChanged: false}}, serverInfo: {name: the imported MCP_SERVER_NAME constant, version: the imported MCP_SERVER_VERSION constant}} whatever version its params ask, and keeps no state; ping answers an empty result object; tools/list answers {tools: [...]} as below, ignoring any cursor; tools/call names the catalogue operation in params.name and carries its request in params.arguments, which then pass the remaining checks of the first note.

answer_request: [FIELD_PROJECTION] tools/list lists one tool per catalogue operation in State 5 catalogue order, each {name: the operation name, inputSchema: the schema of its request model}, derived only by this rule: a model is {"type": "object", "properties": its fields in declared order, "required": its fields not typed X | None, "additionalProperties": false}; str is {"type": "string"}, int {"type": "integer"}, X | None {"anyOf": [the schema of X, {"type": "null"}]}, so the published schema admits the null a request may carry, tuple[X, ...] {"type": "array", "items": the schema of X}, an enumeration {"type": "string", "enum": its members in declared order}, a Literal tag {"const": the tag}, and a discriminated union {"anyOf": the schemas of its variants in declared order}; no description, title or other keyword is added.

answer_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] A refusal decided before the operation is known is a JSON-RPC error response whose error is {code, message: the refusal code, data: the RefusalAnswer as {code, reason}}: a body over the size ceiling is -32600 invalid_request; a token refusal -32600 unauthorized; a body nesting deeper than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant -32600 invalid_request; a body that is not JSON -32700 invalid_request; a body that is not one JSON object — a batch array included — or whose jsonrpc is not "2.0" -32600 invalid_request; a request whose method is none of initialize, ping, tools/list and tools/call -32601 invalid_request; a tools/call whose params is not an object with a string name and an object arguments, or whose name is no catalogue operation, -32602 invalid_request.
judgement.why: The later contracts make all three methods stateless after the common checks, define their exact JSON-RPC results and catalogue order, ignore initialize parameters and tools/list cursors, and specify their protocol-level failures.

topics.topic: Define the own_proc sandbox filesystem, visibility, mount restrictions, access permissions, and audit exemptions
questions: Is the function allowed to read its private `/proc`, and if so which paths or interfaces are exempt from the filesystem audit trap?
What exactly is `own_proc`: which proc filesystem or synthetic process facts are present, where they are mounted, and which processes and fields function code may observe?
What exactly is `own_proc`: where is it mounted, which processes and proc entries are visible, and with what mount restrictions?

quotes: execute_function: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST start bubblewrap with new user, PID, IPC, UTS and network namespaces and no network interface but the new namespace's own loopback, which bubblewrap brings up, with no capability option, the environment cleared and then set exactly to the imported SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT constant, exactly the host paths of the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant bound read-only, inside the new root the symbolic links of the imported SANDBOX_ROOT_SYMLINKS constant (each name linking to its target, made by bubblewrap --symlink), one fresh private exchange directory bound read-write, bubblewrap's own fresh proc mounted at the imported SANDBOX_PROC_MOUNT constant and minimal dev mounts, and no other host directory; the child dies with its parent, and the runner is the init of the new PID namespace (bubblewrap --as-pid-1), so bubblewrap exits only after the host kernel has killed and reaped every other process of that namespace. The interpreter it starts there is os.path.realpath(sys.executable), the kernel's own CPython under a path of the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant, never a launcher such as a virtual environment's.

runner_source: [BEHAVIOR] process_count bounds the code's tasks alive at once: the main thread counts as the first, every live thread and every process forked with os.fork counts with its threads; with the runner as the namespace's init every task the environment's proc lists is one of them, so every listed task counts and none is told apart by its parent. Process creation other than os.fork — subprocess, os.system, os.posix_spawn, os.posix_spawnp and the os.exec family — is subprocess use and raises in the audit hook as a trap hit (A03 rule 4). On os.fork and on starting a thread the audit hook MUST count the tasks by listing the task directory of every process listed in the proc directory its configuration's proc_directory names, opening no file there — an open outside the exchange directory and the readable_paths is itself a trap hit —, and, when the new task would exceed process_count, write a resource hit to the channel and raise, so the execution concludes resource_exhausted even when the code catches the error; a creation the outer limit refuses is reported the same way (A03 required test 2).

runner_arguments: [BEHAVIOR] MUST return exactly two arguments: the decimal number launch.channel_fd, the descriptor the program writes every message to, which is the parent's own pipe end inherited at that number; and one JSON text with the members exchange_directory, code_file, inputs (each port, carriage, cardinality and files), output_ports (each name, carriage and cardinality), and memory_bytes, process_count and output_bytes of launch.bounds; its member file_size_limit is the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant; its member environment is the imported SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT constant; its member readable_paths is the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant; its member raise_on_call is the imported SANDBOX_TRAPPED_FUNCTIONS constant; its member raise_without_argument is the imported SANDBOX_TRAPPED_WITHOUT_ARGUMENT constant; its member raise_on_every_method is the imported SANDBOX_TRAPPED_CLASS constant; its member raise_unseeded is the imported SANDBOX_UNSEEDED_CONSTRUCTOR constant; its member proc_directory is the imported SANDBOX_PROC_MOUNT constant; the program reads exactly these two arguments after its own path.
judgement.why: The later contracts define own_proc as bubblewrap's fresh procfs at the release mount path, visible only for the sandbox PID namespace, while ordinary file opens there remain trapped because only runtime paths and the exchange directory are readable exemptions.

topics.topic: Define authoritative repair-view evidence when repeated trial executions have different outcomes
questions: Can repeated TrialExecutions for the same implementation and case have different outcomes, and if they can, what evidence must the repair view relation expose or treat as authoritative?

quotes: The standard library's own entry points for the clock and for randomness raise in a function, so it cannot depend on the time or on chance by accident; code written to get time or chance some other way is not detected and is judged by its outputs like any other. Every promise in these documents that a function repeats itself — equal outputs on equal inputs, a repaired slot staying repaired, a verdict that holds — is a promise about code whose outputs depend only on its inputs; the kernel neither checks that nor masks any other fact of the process.

trial executions of an implementation on its contract version's corpus | `surface` (repair view) | per case of the current corpus, in corpus order, the implementation's latest TrialExecution M07 in store order — from admission or a try alike, since an outcome depends only on implementation and case; a case never executed is omitted
judgement.why: State 0 now permits repeated executions of input-dependent-plus-untrapped-fact code to differ, while State 5 still asserts that an implementation-and-case pair determines one outcome.

witness.initial: A submitted implementation has one trial case expecting `0` and returns `0` or `1` from an untrapped process fact while receiving the same case inputs.
events: An agent tries the implementation on that case and receives a passing TrialExecution.
The agent tries the same implementation on the same case again and requests the repair view.
outcomes: Under K-02, the second execution may be `output_mismatch`, and the repair view exposes that latest differing TrialExecution.
Under the State 5 relation's assertion that the outcome depends only on implementation and case, the repeated execution has the same passing outcome for that pair.
witness.observer: The agent sees either a latest mismatching execution or a passing execution for the same implementation and case.
basis:

   executes an existing implementation on the cases of its contract version's
   corpus that the request names, all of them when it names none, in corpus
   order, records one TrialExecution per case and returns them.
